title: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_baseChange_of_smooth_of_ring_order_invertible
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring and let f:X→Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and g:Y′→Y smooth. Given a cartesian square with upper map g′:X′→X and left map f′:X′→Y′, assume that for every a∈Λ its additive order, viewed in Γ(Y,top), is a unit. Then the derived étale base-change natural transformation with coefficients in ModuleCat Λ is an isomorphism of functors.

proof.text: For each bounded-below complex K, apply the existing source theorem `Etale.isIso_baseChange_app_of_smooth_of_isTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder` to the smooth leg g and the square with the roles exchanged. Let N = addOrderOf(1 : Λ). If N is nonzero, addOrderOf_nsmul_eq_zero shows (N : Λ) = 0, while the hypothesis at 1 makes N invertible on Y; `of_natCast_eq_zero` therefore supplies the required invertible-order torsion structure on every homology sheaf. If N = 0, the hypothesis at 1 makes 0 a unit in Γ(Y, top), hence that ring is subsingleton and Y is empty. The map f then forces X empty. Every geometric point of X is impossible, so each homology sheaf satisfies the torsion structure vacuously. Thus every component of the module base-change transformation is an isomorphism. `NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app` upgrades these component isomorphisms to the natural transformation. This source theorem proves the bounded-below step by cohomological devissage and truncation, reducing to `Etale.isIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_of_smooth`, the declaration of [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change]. Thus the retained DAG dependency is the smooth base-change theorem actually used by the packaged derived argument; no new intermediate statement is introduced.

proof_origin.note: Direct specialization of the existing bounded-below smooth base-change theorem; the ring-order argument handles both nonzero and zero additive order of 1.
